description:
From: Elixir Parity, found first by Binary Handling. User-approved 2026-11-25 as its own ticket, after #791.

fz_binary_part's only caller is :erlang.binary_part's first clause. That clause's guard proves is_binary(binary) and a byte window, and the runtime call copies or shares whole bytes. So extern "fz" defp fz_binary_part(binary, integer, integer) :: binary is the truthful declaration. It is strictly more precise than :: bitstring and matches binary_part/3's own @spec. It is not needed for correctness: #910 (fz-9e2.17) makes cursors answer type tests.

Done when: lib/erlang.fz declares :: binary, and a test shows binary_part's result is proven binary.
title: fz_binary_part declares binary, not bitstring
